To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the studied poplar genes encoding the components of the ABB route were differentially expressed in response to various stimuli, (2) the light conditions were the most important factor, from among studied stimuli, controlling their expression, (3) the expression of the Pte-RbohD genes was the highest in response to dehydration in poplar buds, (4) the expression of Ptre-Hab1 and Ptre-Hab3a genes was the highest at dark conditions,

(i) poplar SnRK2.1 and SnRK2a protein kinases are the counterparts of the Arabidopsis SnRK2.4 and SnRK2b, respectively, (ii) poplar SnR2.6 protein kinase, the counterpart of Arabidopsis SnR2.2 and 3, is encoded by two genes, and (iii) poplar RbohsD and RbohFs are encoded by two genes each.
the expression of Ptre-RBOH genes is involved in the early response of poplar buds to dehydration and in the dark-induced stomatal closing in poplar leaves.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of poplar counterparts of the components of the ARA route from Arabidopsis, with the expression of the genes encoding these proteins, and the analysis of the effect of various stimuli on this expression.

the expression of genes encoding the components of ABA route in response to various stimuli in poplars, and it may be helpful in the further research on the role of the studied proteins in the ABA route and in the stress-induced stomatal closure in poplars.
the identification of poplar counterparts of some ABA-related genes from Arabidopsis, and with the study of their expression patterns in poplar leaves and buds subjected to various stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the studied genes are expressed in poplar buds, leaves and stems, and their expression profiles are different in the above plant tissues and organs.
the poplars are equipped with a complex network of the genes encoding the ABA route components.
the studied poplar genes encoding ABA signaling components were differentially expressed in response to various stimuli, but their role in stress response and signaling remains to be elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the studied genes are not expressed in response to dehydration in poplar, however their expression is affected by the light conditions or by the ethylene signaling pathway.
the studied poplar genes encoding the ABA signaling route components are expressed in leaves and buds, and their expression is modulated in a stimulus-specific manner.
the studied poplar genes encoding the components of ABA route are expressed in leaves and buds, and that their expression is affected by light conditions and/or dehydration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the poplar genome encodes the counterparts of the ABA pathway components, and that their expression in response to dehydration is different in leaves and buds, and that the studied RbohD and Rboh F proteins are the main source of superoxide anions in dehydrating poplar buds.

the expression of the genes encoding the components of the ABB route may be differentially regulated depending on the tissue, developmental stage or the type of stress, but the role of these components is still not clear.

the poplar genome encodes a set of the components of the ARA route that is similar to the Arabidopsis one, but also includes several proteins that are absent in Arabi-dopsis, or are present there but are not encoded by the poplar genome.
